live_training.question: Does training on operational data close the gap?

A_benchmark_trained_on_benchmark.name: A
A_benchmark_trained_on_benchmark.description: Benchmark-trained on its own chronological test.

B_benchmark_trained_on_operational.name: B
B_benchmark_trained_on_operational.description: Benchmark-trained on the operational era — the gap.

C_operational_trained_on_benchmark.name: C
C_operational_trained_on_benchmark.description: Operational-trained on the benchmark test — does it generalise backwards, or only fit its own era?

D_operational_trained_on_operational.name: D
D_operational_trained_on_operational.description: Operational-trained on the operational test — the best achievable with deployment-era data.

live_training.answer: Operational training changes TSS by -0.136 on the same operational test rows (95% CI -0.255..-0.009). The interval excludes zero BELOW, so training on the newer era measurably HURT — the benchmark-era model generalises to deployment better than a model fitted on deployment-era data. The loss is not a training-data problem, and collecting more recent data would not fix it.
